# INSIGHTS — summarized, verified findings (accumulate across the whole run)

The JOURNAL is your per-iteration diary; THIS file is the distilled, VERIFIED takeaway a future iteration should read instead of re-reading the whole journal or old sessions/traces. Update it whenever you have a genuinely NEW, confirmed finding (an accepted/rejected RESULT counts as confirmation; a guess does not) — not every iteration needs a new entry. Structure each addition as:

    ## <task or mechanism name>
    - What worked (confirmed by a RESULT, cite the candidate id):
    - What didn't (confirmed by a RESULT, cite the candidate id):
    - Promising but not yet tried:

## SpreadsheetBench scorer semantics (what the graded artifact actually is)
- What worked (no RESULT yet — this is trace-verified, not gate-verified): **the scorer
  recalculates Excel formulas before comparing.** Task 42198 scores 1.0 with a final program
  that only ever writes `=IF(COUNTIFS(...))` strings via openpyxl and never computes a value.
  Corollary a future iteration must not undo: do NOT instruct the agent to always write literal
  values instead of formulas — 7 passing tasks (31011, 39515, 41589, 42198, 49801, 52807, 55468)
  pass by writing formulas.
- The real formula defects are narrower than "formulas": (a) **array/CSE formulas** written as
  plain strings evaluate against a single cell, not the array (33722, all 5 cells wrong);
  (b) formulas that can resolve to `#DIV/0!`/`#N/A` are stored as **error text** and never
  equal an expected number (53647, 42354).
- What didn't: n/a (no RESULT yet).
- Promising but not yet tried: the precision/rendering cluster (46646's 0/1/9-decimal rule,
  49036's integer-percent-plus-text, 11842's 1-of-96 near-miss) is untouched by general prose
  and probably needs a worked example of stored-value-vs-number-format.

## SpreadsheetBench agent behavior under the as-shipped default prompt
- Measured over all 40 val trajectories (scripted, reproducible): **38/40 tasks write the graded
  output file in their very first code block**, before any real cell value has been observed;
  only 6/40 tasks ever call `print(`; **0/40 ever re-open `output_path` to check what they
  wrote**; and 16/40 burn all 30 rounds re-sending 25–27 byte-identical blocks. The cause is
  structural, not a knowledge gap: every block ends in a silent `wb.save(...)`, so the harness
  returns `[Code executed successfully with no output]`, which the agent reads as "nothing
  happened" and retries verbatim.
- **Adapter mechanic worth remembering: only the FIRST ```python fence in a reply is executed;
  later fences are discarded unrun.** 41978 (3 fences) and 5835 (2 fences) each put their
  verification block second and silently lost it. Zero passing tasks emit multiple fences.
- `pd.read_excel` → `df.to_excel` is the dominant failure mechanism (10 of 16 failures). It
  regenerates the whole sheet: text→int/date coercion, one-row shifts from header/index
  mismatch, other sheets dropped, `NaN`/`Unnamed: 3` written into cells. The scorer names it
  directly: *"N cells were CHANGED although the expected value is the cell's own original
  input"* and *"int where str was expected — KEEP the original text"*.

## The sheet-name kill (pandas to_excel silently renames the sheet) — REPRODUCED
- Confirmed by direct reproduction, not inference: `pd.read_excel(path, sheet_name='Query')`
  returns a DataFrame that no longer carries its sheet name, so `df.to_excel(out)` writes ONE
  sheet named `Sheet1`. Input `['Sheet1','Query']` → output `['Sheet1']`. When `answer_position`
  names a sheet, the grader looks it up, fails, and scores 0 **before comparing any value** —
  so the agent's numbers can be entirely correct and still score zero.
- **Diagnostic signature to recognize it in feedback:** full/matching COVERAGE counts and **no
  MISMATCH line at all**. That combination means the scorer never got as far as comparing cells.
  Present on 42354 and 51359; 5835 also round-trips a named sheet (`גיליון1`).
- Promising but not yet tried: nothing else needed here — the fix is the openpyxl-in-place idiom
  plus asserting `answer_position`'s sheet is still in `sheetnames` of the file you wrote.

## Round-cap churn is NOT a failure signal (control-group check)
- 30-round churn (61-message trajectories with 25–27 byte-identical consecutive blocks) occurs
  on **11 PASSING tasks vs 7 failing** ones. It is a harness artifact: the loop-break never
  fires while each resubmitted block keeps re-saving the output file. Do NOT spend an iteration
  trying to stop the churn — it is uncorrelated with reward.
- The generalizable method lesson: **compute every candidate failure signal over the PASSING set
  before ranking it.** This control demoted the churn cluster, and the same control (42198
  passing on formula strings alone) prevented a formula ban that would have regressed 7 tasks.

## Premature rounding vs number format
- 46646 applied `round(v, 9)` to full-precision floats and only 2 of 12 values survived; 49036
  wrote `f"{x:.0%} WIN RATE"` as a string. Instruction wording about decimal places, commas, or
  what to "show" describes the **number format** (display); the stored value stays exact, and the
  grader reads the stored value. Round only when the instruction asks for a rounded *value*.
